entities.summary:
Tang Jian (579–656), courtesy name Maoyue, posthumously known as Duke Xiang of Ju, was a Chinese official who lived in the early Tang dynasty and rose to prominence during the reign of Emperor Taizong. He played a key role in the development of the Tang dynasty's legal system, which became a model for later Chinese law. Tang Jian's contributions to the Tang dynasty's administration and governance helped shape the empire's policies and institutions. The legacy of Tang Jian can be seen in the many scholars and officials who followed in his footsteps, including the famous Tang historian, Ouyang Xiu.

Tang Jian was born into a noble family in the Tang dynasty's capital, Chang'an (modern-day Xi'an), and received a traditional Confucian education. He began his career as a low-ranking official in the imperial court and gradually rose through the ranks due to his intelligence, hard work, and dedication to the imperial family. Tang Jian's expertise in the Tang dynasty's legal system and his ability to navigate the complex web of imperial politics made him a trusted advisor to Emperor Taizong.

Tang Jian's impact on the Tang dynasty's administration was significant, as he helped to establish the imperial court's judicial system, which became a model for later Chinese law. He also played a key role in the development of the Tang dynasty's taxation system and its military campaigns. Tang Jian's legacy can be seen in the many scholars and officials who followed in his footsteps, including the famous Tang historian, Ouyang Xiu.
